newsitem.title: UK: Dollar steady in Europe, trade thinned by holidays.
newsitem.headline: Dollar steady in Europe, trade thinned by holidays.

text.p: The dollar was steady against the yen and mark in early Europe, though off overnight highs, with turnover restricted by holidays in London and Tokyo.
"The dollar has been rangebound," said a trader at a Swedish bank, adding that turnover on Monday had been thwarted by holidays in Tokyo and London.
At 0721 GMT dollar/mark was trading at 1.7267/72 against 1.7294 in late Europe on Friday, though off overnight highs just above 1.73 marks.
Against the yen, the dollar was trading at 126.57/6.67 against 126.65 in late Europe on Friday.
Overall, the dollar was in good shape after the release of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls and news of a government agreement to balance the budget by 2002, said traders.
Elsewhere, sterling slipped against the mark, with markets attentive as the new Labour government under Prime Minister Tony Blair begins its first full week of power.

Markets are particularly focused on Wednesday's UK monetary meeting between new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown and Bank of England Governor Eddie George, amid speculation Brown will sanction the interest rate rise the BoE has long been urging.
At 0749 sterling was quoted at 2.7980/90 and $1.6205/11 against 2.8052 and $1.6220 in late Europe on Friday.
